about: The fact kinds this vertical answers for, in the process-global registry (`worldloom.factkinds`) — the fifth registration seam, and the one `lob.lint_responsibilities` and the episode grammar's lint consult. Retail registers the shared vocabularies too: `close.*` and the incident-chain `ops.*` kinds are minted verbatim by banking's and procurement's episodes ("reuses retail's close.* kinds verbatim" — `generators/regulatory.py`), and a kind has one declaration whoever's episode mints it — the other verticals register only what is theirs alone.

fact_kinds.about: The committed close date for the period.
The moved close date, when an incident moves it.
Where the close stands; a delayed status is superseded, never edited.
Business days the close slipped.
Actual revenue; child subjects sum to their parent's figure exactly.
Budgeted revenue, rolled up the same way.
Actual less budget, exactly — validate.financial() recomputes it.
Actual gross profit.
Budgeted gross profit.
Actual less budget on gross profit.
The stated margin, derived from the amounts beside it.
The budgeted margin, same derivation.
The P&L cost the incident is assessed at.
Margin variance in points, for the memo.
Online conversion as landed.
Online conversion as forecast.
What promotional depth took off margin.
The raised ticket.
fact_kinds.note: The incident chain. Shared vocabulary: banking's regulatory episode mints most of these kinds too, against its own incident, under this declaration.

fact_kinds.about: What broke. The confirmed cause supersedes the initial hypothesis; the hypothesis stays on the record as a past belief.
The evidence that dismissed the hypothesis.
The failed feed's state.
Whether inventory valuation completed.
The applied workaround.
Who owns the mapping table — 'unassigned' is the finding.
The named earlier period a comparable failure occurred in.
The audit classification of the failure.
The tickets raised to fix it.
Which remediation addresses the control failure.
The blast radius the ticket quotes.
The corporate cost base, by the cost centre that incurs it; the centres sum to the group figure exactly.
fact_kinds.note: The corporate centre and the distribution network. Both blocks exist because `validate.reachability` measured this vertical's own organisation as decorative: two cost centres declared by every retail company and named by no fact, and — on any archetype with warehouses — an estate of zero-weight sites the store P&L correctly refuses turnover to and nothing else said anything about. `generators/retail_estate.py` opens with the counts.

fact_kinds.about: The same base, by the division it is recharged to. A second decomposition of one figure over a different set of entities, which is what makes either checkable.
Recharge as a share of the subject's own revenue. A rate: stated at every level it is read at and summed at none.
Cartons dispatched through a distribution centre. The measure a site that sells nothing actually owns.
What moving that volume cost, by the centre that moved it.
Cost over volume at the level it is stated. A rate — the network's figure is its own two amounts divided, never the total of its centres' rates.
